name: Dungeon Doors
description:
A door in every doorway. world.floor_descent knows where a corridor meets a room's rim and drew the gap darker; world.door_gate is a passage wired to switches and plates, a puzzle piece, not this. Every crawler since Rogue has doors, and a door is the smallest thing that makes a dungeon feel built rather than generated: closed until something walks into it, open after, and the one on the boss's room locked until a key turns.

This owns the doors: where they are (every doorway of an open corridor, read from the floor), whether each is closed, open or locked, and what style it wears by the room's tag. A unit stepping onto a closed door opens it — any unit, because a goblin that walks through a shut door is a goblin that walks through a wall. A locked door refuses a footstep: the floor's isBlocked asks this, the same way it asks the stamps about a solid prop, so the walker, the pathfinder and the pursuer all get the one answer. The player's unit arriving beside a locked door with the key in the bag unlocks it and the key is spent; without the key the door says so, once per approach. A CLOSED DOOR IS OPAQUE: world.vision_system asks this before it lights a tile or lets a hunter notice anybody, so the room behind a shut door is dark and quiet until it opens. What was opened and unlocked is remembered per floor.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: lockedTags
inputs.description: Room tags whose doors start locked. The boss's room by default: the fight at the bottom of the floor should be the one you went looking for the key to.

inputs.name: keyItem
inputs.description: The carried item a locked door takes, spent on unlocking. Laid on the floor by inventory.ground_items' alwaysLay, or dropped by whatever the request decides.

inputs.name: styleByTag
inputs.description: Which door sheet a room's doors wear, by tag — `wood` or `iron`; anything unnamed is wood. Content, not rule.

outputs.name: doors
outputs.description: Every door on the floor as {x, y, room, tag, style, open, locked}.

outputs.name: isClosed
outputs.description: Whether a closed door stands on a tile — opaque to sight. Asked by world.vision_system.

outputs.name: blocksAt
outputs.description: Whether a LOCKED door stands on a tile. Asked by world.floor_descent from its own isBlocked; an unlocked closed door does not block, it opens.

outputs.name: revision
outputs.description: Bumped when a door locks or unlocks, folded into the floor's revision so the pathfinder rebuilds.

provenance: Asked for by the Dungeon Crawler's second level pass (2026-09-11), from the list of what the first playable floor lacked beside Diablo, Baldur's Gate and Brogue: eleven door sprites drawn and a doorway that was a gap in the rim. Searched first: world.door_gate is a passage wired to switches and pressure plates, world.ability_gate its metroidvania sibling; neither is a door you walk into. Library-native, written against the studio's floor generator, walker and vision.
